Unison UI for macOS 1.0.1

Version 1.0.1 is a maintenance release. It makes opening a profile, retrying after an error and recovering archives behave consistently when a command-line request arrives at the same moment, and it keeps the protection around archives held by an interrupted operation in force until a profile actually opens. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration. Requires macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon.

Fixed

  • A command-line request no longer disturbs a password prompt. If you ran unison <profile> while a password, passphrase or host-key prompt was waiting, the app used to close the window the prompt belongs to and report success without opening anything. It now refuses the request with a message, and the prompt stays where it is until you answer or cancel it.
  • Profiles blocked by an interrupted operation stay blocked until they open. The app checked this only when a request was made. A profile queued behind another session, or waiting on your answer to a synchronization decision, could still open after its roots changed to overlap a held archive. The check now runs again just before the profile opens. A refused open returns to the profile picker with a notice, and a synchronization that is running is left alone. This now includes a profile that has a remote (ssh:// or socket://) root next to a local one. The app cannot tell which archives such a profile uses until it connects, so it stays blocked while any interrupted operation holds archives, and it says why.
  • Rescan Ignoring Archives acts on the session you confirmed it for. If a command-line request replaced that session while the confirmation was open, confirming used to close the replacement and reopen the older profile.
  • Recovery keeps the options a session was opened with. Retry Ignoring Archives, Delete Orphans and Retry, and Rescan Ignoring Archives used to reopen the profile without options such as -path, so the recovery scan could cover the whole profile. They now keep the options, and later reconnects use them too.
  • Retry Ignoring Archives no longer edits your profile file. The setting applies to that one reopen. It also takes effect when the session was opened with -ignorearchives=false, and a recovery you cancel leaves nothing behind.
  • Reset Archives, Delete Profile and the open check follow includes. A profile whose roots live in an included file no longer looks like it has none. When the includes cannot be resolved, the app keeps archives in place and blocks opening while interrupted operations hold archives. A profile file without an extension that has the same name counts as another owner of the archives.
  • The profile picker has a minimum size, and a saved window size that is too small is raised when the picker is restored.

Under the hood

The app now loads the held-archive state before it answers command-line requests, and a recovery reopen checks the held-archive state first. Unused code was removed and several large source files were split, with no change in behavior.

Unison UI for macOS 1.0.0

Unison UI for macOS reaches 1.0 with safer profile management, clearer diagnostics, and a more polished interface, from creating your first profile to reviewing differences and recovering from errors.

Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration. Requires macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon.

Fixed

Deleting a profile now protects synchronization history that other profiles share. Profiles that use the same pair of roots share archive files, and deleting one of them could remove those archives, after which the other profile would forget earlier deletions and could copy a deleted file back. The app now recognizes shared archives, keeps them, and names the profile that uses them. It checks again under the archive lock before it moves anything, and it keeps the archives whenever it cannot tell whether another profile uses them. Reset Archives likewise names the other profiles whose synchronization history it will also reset.

Changed

Warnings and errors. Warnings and failures now lead with a concise summary. The complete diagnostic sits in a scrolling, selectable Details area with a Copy Details button, so long paths stay intact. Warnings offer Continue and Cancel, and restart notices say what to do next.

Profile setup.

  • An empty Profiles window offers a Create Profile… button, or a Manage Profiles… button when every profile is hidden.
  • Run is enabled only while a profile is selected, and long profile names keep their beginning and end, with the full name in a tooltip.
  • A settings search with no matches offers a Clear Search button.
  • Profile names are checked as you type, with the reason shown when a name is not valid.
  • Check Remote Command is unavailable for a profile that has not been saved yet, and the editor says why.

Diff window. The Diff window now names the file being reviewed and, when it can identify them reliably, shows the two files being compared. The full command stays one click away behind a Command… button. For a standalone standard diff command, the result reads "Differences found." instead of "Exited with status 1". Custom commands and pipelines keep the status they reported.

Finishing touches. The reconcile summary uses correct singular wording, help examples display as code, and Archive Maintenance explains what it can clean up. Long Command Line setup paths are truncated in the middle, with the full path in a tooltip.

Added

Help ▸ Star on GitHub, next to Donate, opens the project page, and a linked sentence in the About window notes that a star helps others find Unison UI.

### Fixed

  • Release builds no longer carry code-coverage instrumentation that writes default.profraw when the bundled command or server exits. Release gates now inspect the finished binaries and exercise CLI/server execution without coverage output redirection.
  • Help now opens an offline copy of this app's user manual, including the corrected command-line session documentation, shipped with the app.
